source.title: De-randomized PAC-Bayes Margin Bounds: Applications to Non-convex and Non-smooth Predictors
source.authors: Arindam Banerjee; Tiancong Chen; Yingxue Zhou

record.file_problem: Full paper text is present; no evident truncation or document mismatch.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies the fraction of randomly replaced labels and measures test error and generalization-bound components, but its experiments evaluate the bound rather than reproduce the original fitting study.
record.gate_note: The paper reports its own experiments with random-label fractions from 0% to 50%. It states that training error stays at zero as random labels increase, and reports test error rising. The results for test error and training error are figure-based; exact values by corruption level are not stated in the text. Cited results from Zhang et al. and Neyshabur et al. are not extracted as this study's results.
record.test_reason: The study directly repeats random-label corruption experiments and reports training and test error, bearing on V4 despite its primary focus on generalization bounds. It uses the same experimental method and behavioral measures; Adam and corruption-dependent training budgets are recipe differences.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate but incomplete. The authors conclude that their de-randomized PAC-Bayes bounds trade off effective curvature against weight norm, show the expected qualitative behavior as sample size and label randomness change, and are quantitatively meaningful and non-vacuous in their experiments. They also report zero training error as label randomness increases.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments vary label corruption and train fully connected ReLU networks, but focus on evaluating generalization-bound behavior. They use Adam and change the number of epochs by corruption level; random labels are introduced by replacing a portion of labels uniformly, with tested fractions only through 50%.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, network depth and width, and batch size are varied; the paper reports the same qualitative behavior across the tested MNIST and CIFAR-10 settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Effective curvature, weight norm, margin loss, and the proposed bound increase with label replacement.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed generalization-bound components track increasing label randomness in the tested networks.

record.problems: Random-label results are shown in figures, and the supplied text does not state exact test-error or training-error values by corruption fraction. The random-label sweep only reaches 50%, so it does not establish behavior at fully random labels. Results aggregate repeated runs; MNIST uses 30 runs and CIFAR-10 20 or 10 runs depending on the figure.

untested.parts: Completely random labels, chance-level test performance under full randomization, and fitting without changing training hyperparameters are not tested; replacement stops at 50% and epoch budgets increase.
Measured convergence times and the random-versus-real-label time ratio are not reported. Prescribed epoch budgets do not establish convergence speed.
Fitting shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs.

Replacement above 50%, the fully random endpoint at chance, and the detailed shape between the four measured replacement levels. Retention of signal and memorization of noise are not separately measured.
Effects of adding or removing weight decay, dropout, and data augmentation on random-label fitting and true-label generalization.
Learning trajectories separating acquisition of real patterns from memorization of noisy labels.

missing.what: Additional label-replacement experiments are omitted: MNIST depth 6/width 128, depth 4/width 256, and depth 4/width 512; CIFAR-10 depth 4/width 384 and depth 6/width 256, all with 1,000 examples and batch size 128. Add their test-error results and distinguish the study-wide zero-training-error statement from condition-specific measurements. Exact test-error values cannot be read from the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the record's limits_scope verdict for corruption beyond 50%: this range is untested, not an observed failure. Uniform replacement can preserve an example's original label, so replacement fraction is not the fraction whose labels actually change. The supplied text contains captions but no readable plotted values; conclusions about test error rely on the authors' qualitative descriptions.

versions.untested_parts: The experiments reach at most 50% randomly replaced labels, not a completely random labeling of the training set; they do not test the full V1 setting.
Training time or convergence time for random versus true labels is not measured.
No shuffled-pixel, permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise inputs are tested.
The tested corruption sweep ends at 50%; the 50%-to-100% range is not tested. Exact test-error values at individual corruption levels are not stated in the text.
The study does not compare weight decay, dropout, or data augmentation, nor test their removal.
The study does not measure learning order or compare when real-data patterns and noisy labels are learned.
